definitions.explanation: Physically heavy or weighty. A colloquial variant of 重い that emphasizes the subjective sensation of heaviness.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧、{重|おも}たい。
⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{重|おも}たくて⟦{腕|うで}→腕：01006_ude⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧。
examples.english: The shopping bags are so heavy that my arms hurt.

examples.japanese: ⟦{食|た}べ{過|す}ぎて→食べ過ぎる：21686_tabesugiru⟧⟦{胃|い}→胃：01706_i⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{重|おも}たく⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: I ate too much and my stomach feels heavy.

notes:
A colloquial form of ⟦{重|おも}い→重い：00804_omoi⟧. While ⟦{重|おも}い→重い：00804_omoi⟧ is neutral and used in both spoken and written contexts, {重|おも}たい is primarily spoken and conveys a stronger sense of personal, physical sensation of heaviness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{重|おも}たい (the luggage is heavy)
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{重|おも}たい (one's legs feel heavy)
- ⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{重|おも}たい (one's head feels heavy)

USAGE:
{重|おも}たい sounds more casual and subjective than ⟦{重|おも}い→重い：00804_omoi⟧. Use ⟦{重|おも}い→重い：00804_omoi⟧ in writing, measurements, and objective descriptions. Use {重|おも}たい when expressing how something feels to you personally.
